title: 2-Year Treasury Note auction — the first leg of the January month-end block, two days before the FOMC decision
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-21 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 rows. Row reads `2-Year  NOTE / Announcement Thursday, January 21, 2027 / Auction Monday, January 25, 2027 / Settlement Monday, February 01, 2027`, with NO trailing `R` — and the same PDF's legend reads `R --denotes reopening`, so the absence is Treasury's own new-issue marker, not an inference. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2027-01-21 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-21 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09) and proposed because its proposer is the announcement that sizes it. FOMC POSITION: the 2027-01-26/27 FOMC (federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar, fetched direct this session, HTTP 200) puts this auction at decision-day minus two — the earliest leg of a four-auction block that straddles the meeting. SIZE EXPECTATION $69B, unchanged at every 2-Year auction since 2024-04-23 (27 auctions, 28 months) and identical in all six monthly rows sb0590 publishes; the 2-Year sits in the INVARIANT columns of that table because it is a new issue every month with no reopening cycle to place. DEMAND BASELINE for whoever researches it, from fiscaldata auctions_query pulled this session (n=130 2-Year auctions since 2015 on the robust filter): pool bid-to-cover mean 2.686, sd 0.243; the 19 that auctioned at decision-day minus two averaged 2.652 (z -0.14) — no detectable degradation. Since 2024-05 the 2-Year has never printed below 2.41. THE DATA TRAP THAT HIDES THIS SERIES, reproduced twice this session: neither `security_term` nor `original_security_term` is reliable alone — filtering on `security_term` alone admits the 2-Year FRN rows, and `original_security_term` alone admits seasoned reopenings and is itself mislabelled on 16 note rows; the robust filter is the intersection of the two plus `floating_rate: No` and `inflation_index_security: No`. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
